title: Recombinant monoclonal antibody siltartoxatug versus plasma-derived human tetanus immunoglobulin for tetanus: a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, phase 3 trial
summary: This double-blind phase 3 trial randomized 675 patients with tetanus-prone wounds 2:1 to siltartoxatug 10 mg IM or human tetanus immunoglobulin (HTIG) 250 IU. The primary surrogate endpoint, increase in neutralizing antibody titer of at least 0.01 IU/mL, occurred in 95.4% versus 53.2%; absolute difference 42.3% (95% CI 35.5-49.1; P<.0001). Overall adverse events were similar (38.2% versus 33.9%).
findings: Primary surrogate endpoint occurred in 95.4% with siltartoxatug versus 53.2% with HTIG; absolute difference 42.3% (95% CI 35.5-49.1; P<.0001).
Overall adverse events occurred in 168/440 (38.2%) versus 75/221 (33.9%).
Publisher full text reported allergic reactions in 1/440 (0.2%) versus 2/221 (0.9%).
The trial supports passive immunogenicity but was not powered around clinical tetanus incidence.
comparator: Single intramuscular human tetanus immunoglobulin 250 IU.
population: Patients with tetanus-prone wounds requiring passive immunization, recruited primarily through emergency departments at 28 hospitals in China; 675 randomized.
shortTitle: Siltartoxatug versus HTIG for tetanus prophylaxis
limitations: The primary endpoint was a neutralizing-antibody surrogate rather than clinical tetanus, participants were recruited in China, and manufacturer employees were among the authors. The product was approved in China, but these data do not establish standard-of-care status in the United States.
whyItMatters: A recombinant monoclonal antibody could eventually provide a scalable alternative to blood-derived HTIG for tetanus postexposure prophylaxis. It should not change US ED practice on this evidence alone: clinical tetanus prevention was not the primary endpoint, and regulatory availability outside China was not established in the sources reviewed.
evidenceNotes: Nature Medicine full text and PubMed were reviewed; PMID 40628965, DOI 10.1038/s41591-025-03791-8, published online July 8, 2025. China NMPA approval was verified; no US FDA approval was established in the official-source search, so this record does not present the regimen as a US standard. Targeted correction search identified no correction.
primaryEndpoint: Proportion with an increase in anti-tetanus neutralizing antibody titer from baseline of at least 0.01 IU/mL.
